sodiumleafculling:
Smart leaf culling algorithm for Sodium on 1.21+ 

 What does this do?

This Sodium addon optimizes the performance of leaves, which are typically more costly to render due to their transparency.

Unlike other leaf culling performance mods, this mod injects directly into Sodium's chunk mesh render pipeline and provides a few new modes. The default is "Solid Aggressive," which will make the insides of large blocks of leaves run in solid non-transparent FAST mode, while maintaining the FANCY mode leaves on the outside. This can lead to a sizable performance boost when using shaders in a dense forest. A more traditional "Hollow" culling mode is also available, which greedily culls vertices inside the tree.

Downloads are available for NeoForge and Fabric. It will not be backported.

1.21+上钠的智能叶片剔除算法 这是干什么用的？ 此“钠”附加项优化了树叶的性能，由于树叶的透明度，渲染树叶的成本通常更高。 与其他的叶子剔除性能模组不同，这个模组直接注入到Sodium的大方块网格渲染管道中，并提供了一些新的模式。默认为“Solid Aggressive，”这将使大方块叶子的内部以Solid非透明FAST模式运行。同时保持FANCY模式叶在外部。这可以在稠密的森林中使用着色器时带来相当大的性能提升。还可以使用“空心”剔除模式，该模式会贪婪地剔除树内部的顶点。 NeoForge和Fabric有下载，但不支持后移植。

OrthoCamera
Minecraft Fabric client-side mod. Adds Toggleable & configurable orthographic view mode.

 

 What is this
In the perspective view (the default), objects which are far away are smaller than those nearby. In the orthographic view, all objects appear at the same scale.

Minecraft uses perspective view to draw the world. It gives a first-person feel. 

This mod allows you to enable orthographic view and configure frustum in detail.

- Saving enabled state between client restarts
- X and Y camera scale
- Minimum and maximum view distance (Position of frustum's near and far plane)
- Fix camera (Lock mouse rotation. Allows to play the game normally, but with an orthographic view)
- Fixed camera rotation
- Fixed camera rotation speed (when rotating using hotkeys)

Screencapper

Screenshot previews, uploads and a screenshot manager for Minecraft.

---

 
 
 
 

---

 What it does
In vanilla Minecraft, sharing a screenshot means opening the screenshots folder, finding the file, and copying it somewhere. If the place you're sending it to won't take an image directly, you also have to upload it to an image host first.

With Screencapper, a preview of each screenshot pops up as soon as you take it. You can have it copied to your clipboard or uploaded to your image host automatically, or use the buttons on the chat message to view, copy, upload, open or delete it.

Screencapper needs [OneConfig][oneconfig], and its settings are in the OneConfig menu. It also adds a Screenshots page to the OneConfig sidebar where you can browse, search, copy, upload, open and delete every screenshot you've taken. Run /screenshots to open it.

Imgur works out of the box.

hardcore-lan-commands:
Hardcore LAN Commands

Starting from Minecraft Version 26.2-pre-5 , players can no longer enable commands/cheats when opening a hardcore world to LAN.

Hardcore LAN Commands reverts these changes, allowing players to enable commands/cheats for themselves and others.

 In 26.2 you need to enable commands and enable LAN for the changes to take effect!

 Installation

Hardcore LAN Commands is a client-side mod. It only needs to be installed by the player hosting the singleplayer/LAN world.

Autonomous minecarts

The autonomous minecarts mod allows minecarts to load chunks independently of the player. This allows players to send minecarts over long distances without having to worry about them stopping when they reach the edge of the loaded area.

It works by identifying moving minecarts and adding them to a list of "active" carts. Active carts are each given a chunk ticket which follows the minecart and loads a small number of chunks surrounding it. If a cart stops moving it becomes "inactive" and the chunk ticket is removed after a few minutes.

 Note regarding dimensions: In minecraft versions prior to 1.21.11, dimensions will only tick when a player is present or there are force loaded chunks present. If you are using a version prior to 1.21.11 and want this mod to work in dimensions where no players are present, you will need to force load at least one chunk somewhere in

 Patches sculk shriekers so that they react to redstone-triggered signals 

 What Does This Mod Do?

In the early snapshots for Minecraft 1.19, sculk shriekers could be activated by redstone.
Once the version actually released, however, not only could shriekers only be triggered
by sensors, but sensors that were triggered by any "unnatural" movement (read: not belonging
to the player) would no longer trigger a shrieker.

On the whole this is probably a good thing, otherwise every time a bat spawned in the Deep Dark,

However, not being able to set off synthetic (placed) shriekers with, say, a timer is kind of
a bummer. So this mod patches that behavior so that a shrieker's shriek can be triggered by
 non-player vibrations , allowing players to build:

This mod fixes a series of critical damage multiplier display issues in the Target Dummy mod based on NeoForge's critical hit system API.

The fixed issues include:

Damage numbers with critical damage multipliers could not be displayed on entities other than the dummy.

The critical damage multiplier applied in practice could not be correctly calculated.

For additive damage from other mods, the critical damage multiplier displayed on damage numbers could be incorrectly attributed to other damage sources, such as Apotheosis's elemental damage.

This mod also adds support for Apotheosis's critical hit system, enabling proper critical damage multiplier display.

opencomputers-ii:
OpenComputers II is a spiritual successor to OpenComputers . It carries some of the core ideas with it, such as configurability and sandboxing. However, there are also many changes, such as the mod using actual, emulated hardware.

Computers in this mod run on either a RISC-V or a Z80 architecture, based on the installed CPU. The main onboarding system is OpenOS II, but this also allows running Linux and using it much like you'd use it normally. For example, networking uses an emulated network card and regular ethernet frames, so different Linux computers can communicate just as you'd expect. For the Z80 the mod ships CP/M, for that retro itch.

 Overview
 

The mod provides stationary computers and mobile robots. While computers can connect to other in-world devices via bus cables and extension cards, robots can move through the world and interact with it via installed modules. Computer

respect-world-spawn:
Respect World Spawn

A lightweight mod to help tweak and fix the vanilla behavior of player spawning so that it doesn't override your Y height and rotation(yaw).

Useful for modded servers that want to have a spawn with a roof and facing any direction.

 Usage

Set your world spawn if you haven't already using /setworldspawn and optionally change the spawnRadius gamerule so that players always spawn on the same block: /gamerule spawnRadius 0 

There's two gamerules added by the mod and enabled by default to toggle each of the mod features on/off, you should never need these unless you want the default behavior back for some reason.
- respectSpawnHeight Toggles the fix that prevents the server from positioning the player at the highest altitude block.
- respectSpawnRotation Toggles the fix that provides the spawning logic with the yaw provided to /setworldspawn , as it's bugged on vanilla

Callable Horses

Many popular RPG games have a feature where you can simply press a key and call your horse. Your horse will appear, no matter how far away from it you are.
This mod adds this feature to Minecraft.

 Features

To get a personal horse, you first need to sit on one (works on llamas too!) and press the O key.
If that horse isn't already owned by another player, that horse becomes your personal horse. You can only have one personal horse at a time.
To then call that horse, you need to press the V key. If your horse is near you, it will try to walk to you.
If it is further away it will teleport to you. It can event follow you through dimensions (configurable)!
If your personal horse dies, you can't call it again (also configurable!)

 Calling a horse

- decreasing difficulty if players didn't die

 Command

PathWeaver

 Minecraft works out mob paths on the same thread that runs everything else. This moves that work off it.

Every time a mob decides where to walk, the server thread stops and does the maths. A few hundred mobs
deciding at once is a few hundred searches the tick waits for, and that wait is what you feel.

About

EZ Register GUI is a simple to use tool that aims to help people building redstone computers. It allows you to monitor content of any data register you choose on a configurable GUI.

 Features

- Add as many registers you need
- Manage registers in groups
- Select display mode base (any from binary to hexadecimal)
- Color code
- Select bit length and block spacing
- Save and load profiles
- Render markers in world
- Works with signal strength based memory
- Works with serial data

 How to use

Every command begins with /ez . Run /ezhelp to show all available commands.

 /eztoggle - turns mod on and off.
 
 /ezregister - add register to currently selected group. You need to provide a name then left click the block of the most significant bit. You can specify the bit size, inverted mode, spacing.
 
 /ezgroup - manage groups. See below for details.
 
 /ezremove - remove specified reg

wobblefx:
WobbleFX

WobbleFX is a client-side Fabric mod that adds a springy, exaggerated hit wobble effect to entities in Minecraft.

When a mob gets hit, its model briefly bends, overshoots, and settles back instead of just snapping through vanilla hurt animation. The effect is inspired by cartoony “meme wobble” motion, but implemented as a clean render-only animation layer so it does not affect gameplay.

---

 What it does

- Adds a visible wobble effect when entities take damage
- Uses damped oscillation / spring motion instead of static or linear movement
- Makes hits feel more animated, elastic, and expressive
- Applies the effect visually only on the client

The wobble is designed to feel like:
- a strong initial bend on impact
- a quick overshoot past neutral
- a short settling motion back to normal

---

 Features

Happy Creeper 
Short summary:

Turn creepers into survival companions by weakening, taming, healing, recoloring, and fighting alongside them.

 Overview 
Happy Creeper is a NeoForge mod for Minecraft 1.21.1 that gives creepers a full companion gameplay loop.

Instead of only running from them, you can approach them safely with a creeper head, weaken them with a special biscuit, tame them, and keep them with you as a combat companion.

- Wear a Creeper Head to get close safely.
- Feed the creeper an Anti-Blast Biscuit to weaken it.
- Feed the weakened creeper a Sweet Gunpowder Biscuit to tame it.
- Right-click your tamed creeper with an empty hand to switch between follow and stay.
- Heal it with Gunpowder or another Sweet Gunpowder Biscuit.

DESCRIPTION 
Adds a server-side particle trail to falling blocks such as sand, gravel, anvils, dripstone, and concrete powder. Supports every falling block type, including blocks that don't normally fall. Can help determine the location of a gravity block in cases such as using a dripstone cannon when practicing in singleplayer, where the dripstone moves very quickly and is easy to miss.

 VERSIONS 
Currently supports Minecraft Java 1.21.5 - 26.2

 COMPATIBILITY AND PERFORMANCE 
Incompatible with packs using the same file names. May cause lag in cases with large amounts of falling blocks near the player, or with low memory available, due to the use of function macros applied to all falling blocks every tick. For this reason, it is not recommended to use it in cases such as a superflat world of only gravity blocks. Particles will only be visible within 20 blocks of the player.

 Patreon

📖Introduction📖

 This mod is part of a line called 'Simply', a collection of simple mods that affect the game in simple but considerable ways. 

With numerous mods such as apotheosis, heart canisters, and cyclic around, hearts can easily ascend far past the vanilla amount, with many players even being able to obtain hundreds of hearts. The vanilla void is no longer effective and one can usually teleport or fly out of it with plenty of hearts to spare...

Well this mod aims to change that! Now when you face the void, survival is nearly impossible unless you have an item or ability that grants immunity to void damage. Even if you are playing on vanilla or with only a couple of other mods, Faithful Void can still greatly enhance the experience of falling into the void! AutoPlant automatically plants sapling items on the ground instead of letting them despawn, creating self-sustaining forests with no extra effort.

What it does:

When a sapling item entity is about to expire (using NeoForge's ItemExpireEvent), AutoPlant intercepts the despawn and attempts to place the sapling as a living tree sapling block at that exact location — provided the ground beneath it can support the block. If the placement succeeds, the item is consumed and the sapling takes root. If it can't survive there (e.g., no soil beneath it), it despawns normally.

Why you'd want it:

Chop a tree, and the leaves will slowly drop saplings as usual. Without this mod, those saplings eventually despawn and the forest shrinks. ⚔️ Weighted Armor

 Armor should feel like armor.

After a long, long day, you sit back to play another 2 week phase of Minecraft. However, instead of playing your instance, your game opens up to an unfimilliar title screen... 

"What is this" you ask yourself. Curiousity is eating from within you, so instead of leaving this curs'd game, you instead make a new world. Everything looks normal; the graphics look like a mish-mash between classic and modern textures, there are mods from all the versions that don't seem to complement eachother. 

Little do you know, you have stumbled across the Minecraft purgatory, the outcome of forgotten instances, deleted worlds, structures, mobs, biomes and themes clashing with eachother. 

You are now a part of it. 

 Those who stick their toes into the murky water will be dragged under...

BiomeBetray

BiomeBetray is a lightweight trolling datapack that turns biome transitions into moments of chaos. When a player enters certain biomes (deserts, jungles, swamps, and frozen areas), there is a random chance that two items in their hotbar will silently swap positions with items deeper in their inventory. This happens without any visual or audio cue, leaving players confused when they reach for their sword and pull out a stack of dirt instead :D :D

 How It Works

The effect triggers using scoreboard detection for biome changes combined with item manipulation commands. The randomness is seeded per-player using their position coordinates, ensuring unpredictable but consistent behavior.

Contrition is a companion data pack to my first data pack, Attrition! This pack adds six optional new features to the game that you can toggle on and off whenever you please: 

- Lifesteal allows players to regain maximum health by killing other players
- Lifeshare allows players to share their maximum health with other players
- Revival allows players to revive other players that have lost all of their health
- Alchemy offers a craftable alternative to enchanted golden apples
- Chivalry lets players create chainmail armor that gives maximum health bonuses when worn
- Immunity lets players lose maximum health only when dying to another player

---

 Who is this for?

Contrition is designed for players who want even more ways to customize their survival experience without straying too far from vanilla Minecraft. Most of these features are best experienced in a multiplayer survival environ

anti-xray-pack:
This is a simple resource pack which tries to prevent xray texture packs in 1.15+ when used as a server resource pack. This can be useful if there are no good ore obfuscation methods available for a new version/snapshot yet or if you just want to run a Vanilla server without any mods/plugins but still have some protection.

It works in a way that restores the default models of the ores (in the lite version) or all blocks (in the full one, but that breaks custom models from other resource packs) without overriding any textures of other resource packs. That way only the custom models that make it possible to xray are blocked allowing your players to still use other local packs without xray functionality.

If used as a server resource pack it will always override any other xray pack and apply the normal, non-see through blocks. You can then use a plugin to force server resource packs by kic

Experience Minecraft stripped down to its core: a world made of blocks. This resource pack downscales all vanilla textures to 8x8 using crisp nearest-neighbor interpolation, creating a clean, retro aesthetic that emphasizes scale and architectural form.

---

 The Aesthetic

By lowering texture resolution, the visual presentation shifts in a few distinct ways:

 The world feels larger: With less detail per block, your perspective adjusts. Mountains feel massive, horizons stretch farther, and builds take on a more monumental scale.
 The geometry stands out: When each block face is 8 pixels wide, the grid structure is impossible to ignore. Edges sharpen, highlighting the pure blocky nature of the game.
 Design becomes intentional: Without high-detail textures to rely on, every block placement and color choice matters more.

---

 

---

 Why 8x8?

classic-baby-mob-eyes:
What has changed?
The eye textures of baby mobs have been adjusted to:
- Use the classic two-pixel black-and-white format
- Better match the appearance of adult mobs
- Maintain Minecraft’s original minimalist aesthetic

The changes are subtle and designed to feel fully vanilla-friendly.

 Why was it created?
In Minecraft Tiny Takeover drop, nearly every baby mob feature eye designs that differ from the classic two-pixel black-and-white style used by their adult counterparts. This can create a slight visual inconsistency, especially in vanilla-focused worlds.

This resource pack restores the traditional two-pixel eye design to baby mobs, improving stylistic consistency across age variants.

 Impact on gameplay
This pack is purely visual and does not affect gameplay or mechanics in any way. It integrates seamlessly with vanilla textures and works well in both survival worlds and modpacks.

Summary

Ever wanted your game to look like the minecraft vote videos? Well, with this pack you can! This unofficial pack aims to remake all the game's texture to have that beautiful looking mob vote style.

 FAQ:

 
 Why do all the mobs have weird and glitchy textures? 
 
Since this pack's texture resolution is 1.5x times minecraft's default textures, some mob textures are gonna be glitchy, and you'll need to install OptiFine to fix that.

 

 
 Why does every texture looks blurry? 

If you are using optifine (which you should be, the pack requires it for some features to work) you'll need to go to options video settings quality and then lower mipmapping to 3.
 
 

 
 Is this pack made by mojang?

Azka 3D - Diagonal Rails & Ladders
A resourcepack that adds 3D models for rails and ladders and improves the vanilla rails by:
- Replacing curved rails with OpenTTD-style diagonal rails.
- Unstretching raised rails.

Supports Create mod.
 Credits
Diagonal rails in this resourcepack were inspired by blockerlocker's Diagonal Rails.
 Azka 3D Collection
This pack is part of Azka 3D collection of resourcepacks, all of which follow the same design principles:
- Vanilla+ - Models are modified to improve their level of detail, add depth and sometimes make other changes, while being mostly faithful to the vanilla. Indents and extrusions are either 1 or 0.5 pixel in height, matching the style of vanilla blocks.
- No flickering - To prevent Z-fighting (texture flickering), elements extending beyond the block boundary are marginally offset. Models do not use extrusions along their edges to prevent Z

datamosh:
Digital compression errors woven into the world. 

Datamosh is a post-processing shader that recreates the visual artifacts associated with corrupted MPEG-style video compression. Instead of traditional visual enhancement, the shader deliberately introduces macroblock displacement, color quantization, chroma reconstruction errors, and edge artifacts to emulate the appearance of damaged or mispredicted P-frames. The result is a constantly shifting image where sections of the scene appear to borrow data from the wrong locations, producing a convincing datamosh-inspired aesthetic during gameplay.

 

 

 

---

 ✨ Highlights

 Macroblock Motion Corruption. 
The image is divided into 8×8 pixel macroblocks. Each block periodically generates its own motion behavior and samples pixels from offset locations rather than its original position. Most blocks remain stable, while others drift or sudde

数字压缩错误编织成的世界。 Datamosh是一个后处理着色器，它可以重建与损坏的MPEG风格视频压缩相关的视觉伪影。该着色器不是传统的视觉增强，而是故意引入宏方块位移、颜色量化、色度重建误差和边缘伪影以仿真损坏的或错误预测的P-其结果是一个不断变化的图像，其中部分场景似乎从错误的位置借用数据，在游戏过程中产生令人信服的数据流启发的美学。 --- 亮点 宏方块运动损坏。 将图像分成8 × 8像素的宏方块，每个宏方块周期性地产生自己的运动行为，并从偏移位置而不是原始位置采样像素，大部分宏方块保持稳定，而另一些宏方块则发生漂移或突变.

f3nperm:
Introduction

If you press F3 + N or use the gamemode switcher (F3 + F4) on a Bukkit server with permissions for /gamemode , but without op, your Minecraft client will not allow you to actually change your gamemode. This is because the minecraft client requires to know that you are a server operator. This plugin was built solely to mitigate that issue.

 Usage

Dropping the downloaded jar file in your plugins folder should be enough for everything to work. The plugin will attempt to use ProtocolLib if you have it installed, but should work without it as well.

If you don't want everyone with access to /gamemode to also have access to those debug hotkeys, you can customize that behavior by setting "enable-permission-check" to "true" in the "config.yml" of this plugin. With this enabled, you should be able to give people the f3nperm.use permission to give access to the hotkeys.

iosync:
This plugin synchronizes a player's data across multiple Minecraft server instances. This is especially useful in a BungeeCord setting, where players want a continuous experience moving between multiple server instances.

This is done by copying a player's data file ( world/playerdata/UUID.dat ) to a common directory when they disconnect. On reconnection, on the same server or another, the file is copied in place before the server's processes try to read from it. Effectively, the player's data travels with them.

Multiple groups of synchronization on the same network can be done; for example, all survival servers vs all minigame servers. This is possibly by defining different save directories in the config. All of the servers using the same directory will be put in a common pool to share that data.

One notable exception comes from player positions, which must NOT be shared across server

Description

Want to find out how much heap space your server really needs? Want to check that your hosting provider is giving you what you paid for? Other plugins, such as Essentials, will provided memory statistics, but they're probably not what you really want to know. MemCheck provides the amount of heap used and the total amount of free heap space in real time.

MemCheck adds a /mem command which outputs the amount of used heap in MB and as a percentage of the maximum heap size, and the total free heap in MB. It also provides statistics about the Java "Metaspace" use. As a bonus, the server's current TPS as calculated by Essentials, the CPU load, the average garbage collection time in the previous minute, and the total number of loaded chunks are shown.

QuantumAC
 A lightweight, server-side anti-cheat plugin for PaperMC 1.21.x 

---

QuantumAC is a server-side anti-cheat plugin built specifically for PaperMC. It catches the most common cheats through a combination of movement analysis, packet inspection, combat geometry, and world-state occlusion — without relying on client-side modifications.

All detections happen on the server. There is nothing a cheat client can do about packets that were never sent, or a lagback it never saw coming.

---

 Checks

 Movement
- Flight — detects sustained upward or level movement in air. Lagbacks the player to their last safe ground position.
- Speed — flags horizontal movement beyond vanilla limits, accounting for sprinting, speed potions, ice, soul sand, and post-knockback momentum. Lagbacks on confirmation.
- BoatFly — detects upward boat movement exceeding vanilla physics limits per tick.
